find real x such that for all real y, expression at x is at least the expression at y
and there exists at least one real x achieving that maximal value

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.parent_proof_nl:
Let n > 1 be an integer and let r be a real number with (n - 1)/n <= r < 1.

We first handle integers k with 1 <= k < n. From r < 1, multiplying by the positive integer k gives kr < k. Also, from r >= (n - 1)/n we get
kr >= k(n - 1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k < n, we have k/n < 1, hence k - k/n > k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 < kr < k.
Because k - 1 and k are consecutive integers, any real number strictly between them has floor equal to k - 1. Thus floor(kr) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k < n.

Now take k = n. From r >= (n - 1)/n we obtain nr >= n - 1, and from r < 1 we obtain nr < n. Hence
n - 1 <= nr < n.
Therefore floor(nr) = n - 1.

This proves the stated floor identities.

parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n > 1 and every real r with (n-1)/n <= r < 1, for every integer k with 1 <= k < n, the floor of k times r equals k minus 1; additionally, the floor of n times r equals n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all real numbers r with (n-1)/n <= r and r < 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k and k < n
witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses; all quantities are asserted for given n and r and for every eligible k.
